headline: Shifts grid infrastructure costs to large energy users
short_summary: This bill directs Virginia's primary electric provider to establish rates that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity to customers with 25 MW or more in electric demand, primarily data centers, to prevent these costs from being passed on to other ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, bill patrons (Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. Louise Lucas).
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger proposed amendments to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aimed to shift certain capacity and infrastructure costs from residential ratepayers to high-load data center customers. Critics, including bill patrons, stated that the Governor's changes weakened the explicit cost-shift mechanism, but the General Assembly largely rejected these amendments, sending the original bill back to her desk.

headline: Mandates data center water usage reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires water users providing water to data centers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water consumed to the State Water Control Board monthly, enhancing transparency on water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, Potomac Conservancy, local communities concerned about water resources.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/scrutiny).
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills in the past week to regulate data centers, including efforts to track how much water they're using. SB 553 specifically mandates water users providing water to data centers to report their consumption to the State Water Control Board, with a delayed effective date of January 1, 2027.

headline: Establishes local data center siting and noise rules
short_summary: This bill allows localities to require site assessments for high energy users, such as data centers, when applying for permits, enabling local governments to better evaluate and mitigate impacts like noise on surrounding communities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Delegate Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry (due to potential restrictions on development).
news_headline: As data center noise concerns grow, Loudoun Co. officials discuss possible mitigation efforts.
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are experiencing significant noise pollution from a data center, highlighting growing community concerns about data center impacts. HB 153 allows localities to require site assessments for proposed data centers, including sound profiles, to address these quality-of-life issues.
